unit.title: The Many Values of “se”
unit.subtitle: Reflexive, reciprocal, impersonal, passive, accidental and emphatic se

grammar.title: One little word, six different jobs
grammar.intro: The particle se is the busiest word in Spanish. The same three letters mark a reflexive action (se lava), a reciprocal one (se abrazan), an impersonal statement (se vive bien aquí), a passive-reflexive (se venden pisos), an accidental mishap that quietly deflects blame (se me cayó), and an emphatic flourish of totality (se comió toda la tarta). Telling them apart — and building the accidental one correctly — is a hallmark of near-native control.

sections.heading: Reflexive vs reciprocal se
sections.body: With a reflexive se the subject acts on itself (se lava = washes himself). With a reciprocal se two or more subjects act on each other (se abrazan = they hug one another). Only context or a tag like el uno al otro / a sí mismo disambiguates them.
conj: se ayudan el uno al otro

ex.es: Se lava las manos antes de comer.
ex.en: He washes his hands before eating.

ex.es: Los viejos amigos se abrazaron al reencontrarse.
ex.en: The old friends hugged (each other) when they met again.

sections.heading: Impersonal se vs passive-reflexive se
sections.body: Impersonal se hides a generic “one / people” and the verb stays in the singular (se vive bien aquí). The pasiva refleja looks identical but has a real grammatical subject, so the verb agrees with it (se venden pisos, plural). Rule of thumb: if there is a noun that could be the thing acted upon, make the verb agree with it.

ex.es: En este pueblo se vive de maravilla.
ex.en: In this town people live wonderfully.

sections.heading: The accidental se: “it happened to me”
sections.body: To present a mishap as beyond your control, Spanish uses se + an indirect-object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/os/les) + a verb that agrees with the thing, not with you: se me cayó el vaso (the glass fell on me), se le rompió (it broke on him). If the thing is plural, the verb goes plural too: se me olvidaron las llaves. This structure elegantly shifts the blame off the person.

ex.es: Se me cayó el vaso y se hizo añicos.
ex.en: I dropped the glass and it shattered.
ex.note: verb agrees with vaso, not with me

ex.es: Se me olvidaron las llaves dentro del coche.
ex.en: I forgot the keys inside the car.

sections.heading: The emphatic dative se: totality
sections.body: An optional dative se can be added to certain transitive verbs to stress that the action was carried out completely or with relish: se comió toda la tarta (he polished off the whole cake), se lo sabe todo (he knows it all), se leyó el libro entero. The subject is still the doer; the se just adds emphasis and a sense of consumption/totality.

ex.es: No dejó ni un trozo: se comió toda la tarta él solo.
ex.en: He didn't leave a single piece: he ate the whole cake by himself.

takeaways: Reflexive = acts on self (se lava); reciprocal = on each other (se abrazan).
Impersonal se keeps the verb singular; pasiva refleja agrees with its subject (se venden pisos).
Accidental se: se + me/te/le… + verb agreeing with the thing (se me cayó / se me olvidaron).
Emphatic dative se adds totality: se comió toda la tarta, se lo sabe todo.

mistakes.why: In the accidental se the verb agrees with the thing (llaves), not with you: olvidaron, never olvidé.

mistakes.w: Ayer caí el vaso al suelo.
mistakes.r: Ayer se me cayó el vaso al suelo.
mistakes.why: For an accidental drop, Spanish uses se + me + a verb agreeing with the object, not a plain transitive caí.

mistakes.w: Se vende pisos en el centro.
mistakes.r: Se venden pisos en el centro.
mistakes.why: The passive-reflexive must agree with its plural subject: se venden pisos, not se vende pisos.

exercises.prompt: A Marta ___ las llaves dentro del coche.
exercises.prompt_en: Marta accidentally left the keys inside the car.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! El verbo concuerda con “las llaves” → olvidaron.
exercises.no: The accidental se agrees with the thing (las llaves, plural) and uses le for one person: se le olvidaron.

exercises.prompt: No dejó ni una miga: ___ toda la tarta él solo.
exercises.prompt_en: He didn't leave a single crumb: he devoured the whole cake by himself.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! El se enfático subraya la totalidad → se comió.
exercises.no: One subject (él) devouring the lot takes the emphatic dative se: se comió toda la tarta.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I dropped the glass (it slipped from me).”
exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! se + me + cayó (concuerda con el vaso).
exercises.no: Accidental se: “Se me cayó el vaso” — singular vaso → cayó, and me for the affected person.

exercises.prompt: En la costa ___ construyeron cientos de casas en los años sesenta.
exercises.prompt_en: On the coast, hundreds of houses were built in the sixties.
exercises.hint: Passive-reflexive: the particle + a verb agreeing with the plural subject.
exercises.no: Houses were built = passive-reflexive: “se construyeron cientos de casas”.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence to the value of “se” it uses.
exercises.ok: ¡Excelente! Distingues los valores de “se” a la perfección.

exercises.tts: Se me cayeron todos los papeles al suelo.
accepted: se me cayeron todos los papeles al suelo
exercises.translation: I dropped all the papers on the floor.
exercises.ok: ¡Correcto! “Se me cayeron todos los papeles al suelo.”
exercises.no: It was: “Se me cayeron todos los papeles al suelo.” (plural papeles → cayeron).

exercises.scenario: Your boss asks why the report isn't ready 📄

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.es: ¿Por qué no trajiste el informe a la reunión?
lines.en: Why didn't you bring the report to the meeting?

options.text: Lo siento, se me olvidó por completo.
Lo siento, se me olvidé por completo.
Lo siento, me se olvidó por completo.

exercises.ok: ¡Perfecto! Accidental se: se me olvidó (deflecta la culpa con naturalidad).
exercises.no: Accidental se needs a 3rd-person verb and the order se me: “se me olvidó”, not olvidé nor “me se”.

exercises.say: Se me olvidaron las llaves otra vez.
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “Se me olvidaron las llaves otra vez.”

vocab.en: he ate the whole cake (emphatic se)
